1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built.
17	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
18	>   from protected target statements.
19	
20	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
21	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
22	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
23	
24	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
25	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
26	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
27	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.
28	
29	## Repository Layout
30	
31	| Path | Role |
32	| --- | --- |
33	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` | Cleaner curve-specialized AJC route and workspace default. |
34	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme AJC route (Milne–Kollár representability), maintained by scoped tasks. |
35	| `SubProjects/` | Supporting, extracted, and related-paper formalizations available to the active project. |
36	| `references/` | Shared mathematical sources and retrieval notes. |
37	| `.archon-horizon/` | Workspace state: tasks, roadmap, inbox, run metadata, graphs, and ledger. |
38	| `config.yaml` | Ordered workspace manifest. The rebuild is listed first because it is the primary project. |
39	
40	Each route has its own overview:
41	
42	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md)
43	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md)
44	
45	## Project Map
46	
47	The workspace currently registers these projects, in priority order:
48	
49	| Project | Purpose |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| **`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`** | Cleaner curve-specialized route; default project in the workspace manifest. |
52	| `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme, `Pic^0`, and Albanese route. |
53	| `Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso` | Extracted line-bundle pullback, tensor, and dual comparison infrastructure. |
54	| `Albanese` | Albanese universal property, rigidity, and rational-map-extension infrastructure. |
55	| `Cech-Cohomology` | Čech computation of higher direct images and its cohomological substrate. |
56	| `GR-Quot-Closure` | Relative Grassmannian and quotient-representability infrastructure. |
57	| `MR0555258-Compactifying-Picard` | Compactifying the Picard scheme (D'Souza), under `SubProjects/RelatedPapersFormalisation/`. |
58	| `Picard-IdentityComponent` | Extracted Picard identity-component and `Pic^0` development. |
59	
60	These member projects remain useful sources of proved APIs, mathematical designs, and failure
61	memory for both main routes.
62	
63	## Working in a Main Project
64	
65	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
66	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:
67	
68	```bash
69	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
70	lake build
71	```
72	
73	The rebuild uses the shared workspace package directory at `.lake-packages`, so member projects
74	can reuse the same Mathlib checkout while retaining independent build directories.
75	
76	For workspace-wide exploration, run commands from the repository root:
77	
78	```bash
79	horizon dashboard
80	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
81	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
82	```
83	
84	The first command starts the local dashboard. The graph command shows the ranked proof frontier
85	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
86	
87	## Methodology
88	
89	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
90	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
91	
92	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
93	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
94	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
95	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
96	  ranked frontier for each project.
97	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
98	  failure memory.
99	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
100	  and session views.
101	
102	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
103	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
104	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
105	session's uncommitted imports.
106	
107	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
108	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
109	timeless account of the mathematics.
110	
111	## Contributing
112	
113	Contributions are welcome, but keep the two routes and task scope explicit:
114	
115	- **AJC proofs and infrastructure:** change only the main project named by the task; share reusable
116	  inputs through the supporting projects when appropriate.
117	- **Protected statements:** do not alter the signatures in the rebuild's `Challenge.lean` or files
118	  covered by `archon-protected.yaml` without prior agreement. Contributions should discharge those
119	  statements, not weaken or reshape them silently.
120	- **Issues and discussions:** include the declaration name and file path, and state whether the
121	  question concerns the statement, naming, proof strategy, or intended use.
122	- **Large changes:** check the live dashboard or open an issue first so work does not duplicate an
123	  active Horizon task.
124	- **Supporting work:** a focused subproject under `SubProjects/` is appropriate when a reusable
125	  dependency needs to be developed independently, but its intended consumer should be the active

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
21	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
22	
23	## State (measured 2026-07-27)
24	
25	- **168 modules, 122,250 lines.**  **26 `sorry`** remain, spread over 11 modules;
26	  the rest are locally sorry-free.
27	- A warm `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` is **green**: 8,723 jobs, exit 0.
28	- **Locally sorry-free is not axiom-clean.**  Two `sorry`-bodied *instances* leak
29	  through typeclass synthesis: `instHasPicScheme`
30	  (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the sole producer of `HasPicScheme`) and
31	  `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
32	  (`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`).  A theorem that merely
33	  *quantifies over* such a gate reports clean axioms, because the hypothesis is
34	  discharged by the caller; the leak appears at any call site that must
35	  synthesise the instance.  Run
36	  [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean) (`lake env lean
37	  scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`, ~12s warm) before believing any completeness
38	  claim — it measures the frontier rather than inferring it.

40	  build cost and is being converted bottom-up with the helpers in `scripts/`.

2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
21	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
22	
23	## State (measured 2026-07-27)
24	
25	- **168 modules, 122,250 lines.**  **26 `sorry`** remain, spread over 11 modules;
26	  the rest are locally sorry-free.
27	- A warm `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` is **green**: 8,723 jobs, exit 0.
28	- **Locally sorry-free is not axiom-clean.**  Two `sorry`-bodied *instances* leak
29	  through typeclass synthesis: `instHasPicScheme`
30	  (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the sole producer of `HasPicScheme`) and
31	  `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
32	  (`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`).  A theorem that merely
33	  *quantifies over* such a gate reports clean axioms, because the hypothesis is
34	  discharged by the caller; the leak appears at any call site that must
35	  synthesise the instance.  Run
36	  [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean) (`lake env lean
37	  scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`, ~12s warm) before believing any completeness
38	  claim — it measures the frontier rather than inferring it.
39	- Many modules still open with a bare `import Mathlib`; this is the dominant
40	  build cost and is being converted bottom-up with the helpers in `scripts/`.
41	
42	## Open decision
43	
44	Whether to represent the plain relative Picard functor while carrying a
45	`k`-rational-point hypothesis — strictly weaker than the challenge statement,
46	since such a curve need not have a rational point — or to étale-sheafify and drop
47	the hypothesis, is an open decision for the project owner (roadmap
48	`AJC.picrep.rational-point`).  Both branches are recorded in the blueprint's FGA
49	chapter and at the Lean leaf `hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral`
50	(`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`); neither is assumed.
51	
52	Cones closed: `AJC.substrate`, `AJC.linebundle`, `AJC.grquot`, `AJC.cech`.
53	Cones open: `AJC.fbc` (flat base change, three leaves), `AJC.rr`, `AJC.picrep`
54	(Picard representability), `AJC.pic0av` (Pic⁰ is an abelian variety),
55	`AJC.albanese`.  Run `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.jacobian` for the live tree
56	— the roadmap, not this file, is the authority on status.
57	
58	## Navigation
59	
60	- [`AlgebraicJacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian.lean): project import root.
61	- [`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean): the final
62	  Jacobian witness interface and assembly point.  The witness is built from
63	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}`; what remains open is three named leaves stated there.
64	- [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean): the axiom-frontier
65	  probe, and the reachability measurement in its header.
66	- [`blueprint/web/index.html`](blueprint/web/index.html): generated mathematical blueprint.
67	- [`analogies/README.md`](analogies/README.md): index to the historical design notes.
68	- [`../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md):
69	  the alternative Rebuild route.
70	
71	## Layout
72	
73	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/`: sheaf cohomology, the finite-cover Čech
74	  complex, higher direct images, and flat base change.
75	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/`: line bundles, relative Spec, the relative Picard
76	  functor, Grassmannians, Quot schemes, flattening stratification, and Picard
77	  identity components.
78	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/`: rigidity and extension of rational maps, plus the
79	  Albanese factorization.
80	- `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/`: divisor and adelic Riemann–Roch infrastructure.
81	- `blueprint/src/chapters/`: the mathematical blueprint.
82	- `hgraph/`: the generated statement/declaration dependency graph.
83	- `scripts/`: import-minimization and budget-trimming helpers (`min-imports.sh`,
84	  `deumbrella.sh`, `deumbrella-wave.sh`, `trim-budgets.sh`).  They drive
85	  `lake env lean`, never `lake build`, so they do not invalidate the build tree.
86	- `informal/`, `memory/`, `analogies/`: campaign plans, durable notes, and
87	  historical design notes.  See each directory's own index.
88	- [`../../references/summary.md`](../../references/summary.md): shared source
89	  bibliography and retrieval notes.
90	
91	## Build
92	
93	Lean and Mathlib are both pinned at `v4.31.0`.
94	
95	```bash
96	lake exe cache get
97	lake build
98	```
99	
100	For faithful checks, prefer the configured module target.  `lake env lean <file>`
101	does not apply every option from the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` — in particular
102	`maxSynthPendingDepth` — so a direct-file-only instance-synthesis failure can be an
103	option mismatch rather than a source regression.  Files that rely on that option
104	carry a local `set_option` so direct-file, LSP, and module checks agree.
105	
106	This project is part of an Archon Horizon workspace.  Roadmap, task, inbox, and
107	cross-project state live at the workspace root and are reached through the
108	`horizon` CLI.

**Goal:** `cech_computes_higherDirectImage` — for a separated quasi-compact `f : X ⟶ S`,
a quasi-coherent `F`, and a finite affine open cover, the cohomology of the relative Čech
complex computes `Rⁱf_* F`. Unconditional (no enough-injectives appeal).

- [x] **Combinatorial / free Čech engine** — alternating coface complex, homotopy contraction, exactness
- [x] **Section Čech complex & localization comparison** — `AwayComparison`, `phi/phiL` naturality
- [x] **Affine acyclicity (Serre vanishing)** — tilde-vanishing ⇒ affine Čech vanishing
- [x] **Cover/nerve combinatorics** — Čech nerve, wide pullbacks, `pushPull` sigma iso, finitary-extensive distributivity
- [x] **Quasi-coherence on opens** — over-equivalences, restrict-to-basic-open, modules-over-opens equivalence
- [x] **Higher direct image & acyclicity** — injective resolutions, horseshoe lemma, pushforward acyclicity
- [x] **PushPull functoriality** — `pushPullMap` composition, leg coherence, pentagon
- [x] **Comparison theorem `cech_computes_higherDirectImage`** *(proved iter-079, 0 sorries)*

## Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso  *(✅ complete — sorry-free; deliverable merged → AJC)* ✨

**Goal:** the comparison-isomorphism substrate giving `Pic♯_{C/k}` its abelian-group
structure (the A.1.c.sub package; merged back into the Jacobian challenge).

- [x] **Stalk-tensor / internal-hom machinery** — `TensorObjSubstrate/StalkTensor`, `PresheafInternalHom`
- [x] **Slice-dual transport iso (DUAL route)** — `TensorObjSubstrate/DualInverse`, `DualInverse/SliceTransport`
- [x] **Line-bundle pullback / relative Pic functor** — `LineBundlePullback`, `RelPicFunctor`
- [x] **Terminal comparison inverse** — `TensorObjInverse` closed, including the keystone `trivialisation_restrict_compat` ✨

## Albanese  *(prover stage — extraction → Jacobian, 11 open `sorry`)* ✨

**Goal:** the Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰` (Milne III §6 Prop 6.1, seed
`thm:albanese_universal_property`) and the rational-map-extension machinery feeding the
abelian-variety leg of the Jacobian challenge. Extracted from `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`
on 2026-06-20; merges back. *(Full `lake build` green — the carve had dropped load-bearing
base-scheme grading / `Over` / standard-smooth instances, restored from the parent ✨
2026-06-20.)*

- [x] **Auslander–Buchsbaum / coheight bridge** — `Albanese/AuslanderBuchsbaum`, `Albanese/CoheightBridge` **sorry-free**
- [x] **Rigidity lemma + structure-sheaf module substrate** — `RigidityLemma`, `Cohomology/StructureSheaf*` **sorry-free**
- [~] **Albanese universal property** — `Albanese/AlbaneseUP` (×7): the headline `Pic.albaneseUP` + universal-map descent

  reference survives in AJC; only two docstrings record it as a rejected route. `PrimeDivisor` /
  `order` were carved out and kept, per inbox `I-0106`, because codim-one depends on them.

## GR-Quot-Closure  *(✅ complete — sorry-free, deliverable merged → AJC ✨ 2026-06-22)*

**Goal:** representability of the relative Grassmannian — the Čech-independent (H⁰) leg that
builds `Grass(V, d)` from affine charts via the `GL_d` cocycle and proves it represents the
rank-`d`-quotient functor. **Merged back into `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`** ✨ 2026-06-22.

5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,

29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.

7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
24	which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).

26	## Structure
27	
28	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` — the single, reviewable **statement file**: every signature a
29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
30	- `AlgebraicJacobian/` — the infrastructure that discharges the statement (added as the rebuild
31	  proceeds; house limit 500 lines per file, currently exceeded by 14 files tracked in inbox
32	  `I-0220`; layout mirrors the mathematical structure of the paper).
33	- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the library root import list, and the index of what is actually
34	  checked: `lake build`'s default target is this module, so a new file is **not** elaborated by a
35	  bare `lake build` until it is imported here. Add the import, or check the file explicitly by
36	  module name. **This gap is large, not hypothetical:** 624 `.lean` files exist under
37	  `AlgebraicJacobian/` and the root imports 499, so ~125 modules are never kernel-checked by a
38	  bare `lake build`. An unrooted module looks green because no job runs it — see inbox `I-0361`
39	  (the tracked list) and `I-0362` (why it bites). Check the root before trusting a "landed" claim.
40	- `informal/` — 76 design worksheets, brick specs, and recon dumps (~26k lines). **Start from
41	  [`informal/README.md`](informal/README.md)**, which says what each file is for and which are
42	  superseded; several are pinned to routes that have since been abandoned.
43	- `blueprint/` — a clean **mathematical** blueprint (no Lean code in the prose; nodes carry `\lean{}`
44	  and `\source{}` anchors). Build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web`.
45	- `archon-protected.yaml` — the mathematician-owned signatures agents must not modify.
